Q: How to get file MIME type information? A:

(Too long for a readable comment.)

It is much quicker to pass the mimetype call a list of files rather than calling it once for each iteration of the glob loop. For example,

set sep " "
set l [lsort -dictionary [glob -nocomplain *]]` 
set m [exec mimetype --dereference --brief --output-format "{%m {%d}}" --separator $sep {*}$l]
foreach g $l md $m { ... }

With --output-format you can get the MIME type and the description in the same run.

Certain file types take longer to "sniff"; and, for the worst in my directory tests, what was taking over ten seconds now completes in under two. Two examples are a folder of 479 JPEG images which are document page scans and a folder of 264 mp3 files--both took over ten seconds and now complete in under two. Most directories complete very quickly.

I'm not sure how it would work if you had to use the -directory option with glob. There would be more to text in each name to process when sorting and if use -tails to get only the file name, something will need done to get the right file list to mimetype and, in my case, to stat also.

It was easier to just set pwd [pwd] and then cd to the directory of interest and then cd $pwd when complete.

I've yet to try the same for a Windows OS using the suggestion of @JohnBayko because I first need to find a machine running it to test it on.

Q: How to send SCAN_REQ to only one specific BLE sensor on Android — is it even possible? A:

  1. Android makes use of vendor specific hardware filter, if available. Otherwise, the filtering is done on the host side.

  2. If the hardware filter above is in use, there should be no SCAN_REQ sent to irrelevant devices.

  3. No.

  4. If the devices are bonded, you can use the Resolving List feature, if available, combined with the Filter Accept List, in the advertising device. That will make the device not respond to SCAN_REQ with SCAN_RSP for devices not in the list.

But I think filtering at the advertising device is a bit overkill; you will probably not save that much battery usage, if that is what you are trying to minimise.
